options: A proprietary format for compressing database backups
An open protocol for secure data sharing in which recipients use their own compute power
A nightly batch job that copies data to partner organisations
A technique for masking personal data before export
A standard for naming countries in international transactions
questions.explanation: Delta Sharing is an open protocol for secure data sharing: you share your data with others, and the others use their own compute power.

questions.stem: In Delta Sharing, where does the shared data remain?
options: In the original datastore, accessed by recipients without data movement
On the recipient's own servers after a full copy
On removable media couriered to the recipient
In a public download site
In the recipient's email inbox
questions.explanation: Delta Sharing allows recipients to view data without data movement; the data remains in the original datastore and is accessed with the proposed access management.

questions.stem: Why has transferring large volumes of data to other organisations become impractical in the current era?
options: Because networks no longer support file transfer
Because data has become worthless to other organisations
Because data has grown exponentially and organisations do not want it to leave their datastores due to data sovereignty
Because regulators now forbid any form of data sharing
Because databases can no longer export data
questions.explanation: Data has grown exponentially, so transfer is not possible or not timely, and because of data sovereignty organisations do not want their data to move out of their datastores.

questions.stem: In the preceding era, why was giving outside parties access to an organisation's own environment kept very limited?
options: Because outside parties did not have internet access
Because encryption had not yet been invented
Because sharing data was illegal at the time
Because access to the environment and databases impacted performance and applications, which was not acceptable
Because the organisations did not own the data
questions.explanation: Accessing the organisation's environment or databases used to impact performance and applications, which was not acceptable, so access was granted only on a very limited basis.

questions.stem: What practice arose in the earlier era because giving outsiders access to live databases hurt performance?
options: Deleting data after each quarter
Storing data only in memory
Refusing all data requests
Publishing data on public websites
Masking or anonymising data and exporting the actual data to other datastores
questions.explanation: Because direct access hurt performance, organisations started masking or anonymising data and exporting actual data to other datastores.

questions.stem: Whose compute power is used when a recipient accesses data through Delta Sharing?
options: The recipient's own compute power
The data owner's compute power
A neutral third party's compute power
A government-run data centre
No compute power is needed
questions.explanation: In Delta Sharing the recipients use their own compute power, so each party can spin up compute based on their own budgeted OPEX.

questions.stem: How is the data presented to recipients under Delta Sharing?
options: As a complete unrestricted copy of every table
Only their relevant data, in encryption mode, with governance and compliance requirements in place
As printed reports posted by mail
As anonymised summary statistics only
As raw log files with no access controls
questions.explanation: Recipients are only able to see their relevant data in encryption mode, with all governance and compliance requirements in place.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a form of data sharing mentioned?
options: Sharing across departments
Sharing across branches
Sharing across organisations
Sharing with the open wide world in a DaaS model
Sharing by deleting the data from the source
questions.explanation: Data sharing is described as sharing across departments, branches, organisations or with the wide world in a DaaS model; deleting data from the source is not a form of sharing.

questions.stem: Under Delta Sharing, how can each party fund its access to relevant data?
options: By paying the data owner a fixed licence fee for compute
By sharing the data owner's hardware for free
By spinning up their own compute power based on their own budgeted OPEX
By buying the data outright
By using a government subsidy
questions.explanation: With Delta Sharing everyone can spin up their own compute power based on their own budgeted OPEX to access the relevant data.

questions.stem: What opportunity gave rise to Delta Sharing?
options: The need to store more data in fewer datastores
The need to convert SQL databases to NoSQL
The need to eliminate data governance
The need to give access to an environment without using the owner's compute power, letting recipients use their own
The need to print data for archival
questions.explanation: The opportunity was how to give access to the environment without using the owner's compute power, letting the recipient use their own; Delta Sharing answers that need.
